defect_1_unsafe_raw_record_dedup.flaw: R4.3.2's build_census()/normalize() deduplicated typed_semantic_records by record_id() alone (dedup_by(|a,b| a.record_id() == b.record_id())). record_id (SemanticRecordId) is the semantic CLAIM identity -- derived only from a family's identity_key(), which deliberately excludes which extractor produced the observation. Two independent extractors legitimately reporting the SAME semantic claim would get the SAME record_id, so the old dedup would silently erase one extractor's observation -- a direct violation of .atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-EXTRACTION.md#multi-engine-extraction ("Independent extractors MAY analyze the same dimension. Their identities/evidence remain separate ... one extractor may not overwrite another") and of .atlas/contracts/NORMALIZATION.md's RawRecordId != NormalizedRecordId distinction, which R4.3.2 had not actually implemented despite claiming the invariant.
defect_1_unsafe_raw_record_dedup.fix: New RawObservationId (core/src/identity/mod.rs) and SemanticObservation::raw_observation_id() (core/src/semantic/observation.rs): a content hash over claim identity + extractor id/version + epistemic status + evidence_refs + provenance + the full typed payload (via Debug-formatting the Subject, since e.g. FunctionSignature's identity_key() does not range over every field like parameters/generics/abi). Only a byte-for-byte identical raw observation shares a raw_observation_id. record_id() itself is untouched -- no identity_key() function was modified -- keeping the semantic claim identity and the raw observation identity as two distinct, independently addressable concepts, exactly as the milestone required ("Do NOT solve this by simply adding extractor id into every semantic identity key").

defect_2_obligation_lineage_not_canonica.flaw: R4.3.2 preserved CensusReport.evidence/diagnostics, but the full relation an obligation represents (artifact + extractor + dimension + status + which observations/evidence/diagnostics justify it) lived only in the runtime-local CensusExtractionAccounting, never in a serialized canonical report. A SystemizeReport could contain a diagnostic and a compatibility SemanticObligation fact saying "artifact X, SYMBOL, UNKNOWN" with no durable typed record connecting that status to the extractor/evidence/diagnostics that produced it.
defect_2_obligation_lineage_not_canonica.fix: New SemanticObligationRecord (core/src/semantic/obligation.rs): obligation_id is a coordinate identity (hash of repository/revision/artifact/extractor/dimension) -- the natural primary key an ObligationResult already has by construction (ExtractionBatch::is_closed() guarantees exactly one ObligationResult per requested dimension per batch; extract_semantics produces at most one batch per (artifact, extractor) pair). CensusReport/NormalizationReport gained typed_obligations: Vec<SemanticObligationRecord>, populated from the same ExtractionBatches that already feed typed_semantic_records, so the canonical Census can now answer which extractor evaluated which dimension for which artifact at which revision, with what status, backed by which observations/evidence/diagnostics, without the original transient ExtractionBatch[].

defect_3_closure_not_typed_aware.flaw: CensusReport::is_closed()/NormalizationReport::is_closed() only checked counts on the compatibility facts projection (facts_total == facts.len()). A bug that silently dropped a typed record while leaving facts untouched would still report is_closed() == true.
defect_3_closure_not_typed_aware.fix: New TypedClosureAccounting (typed_observations_total, typed_obligations_total -- the same stored-total-vs-live-length pattern facts_total already used) on both reports, plus CensusReport::typed_semantics_closed()/NormalizationReport::typed_semantics_closed(): count checks (stored total vs live Vec::len()) AND referential-integrity checks (every observation's evidence_refs, every obligation's evidence_refs/diagnostic_ids/observation_ids, resolve within the same report's evidence/diagnostics/typed_semantic_records). is_closed() now ANDs this in, so a dropped typed record or a dangling reference flips is_closed() to false regardless of what facts_total says. facts_total's doc comment now explicitly states it is compatibility/report accounting only, never the canonical measure of semantic completeness.

defect_4_graph_still_reads_compatibility.flaw: build_system_graph created its SYMBOL/TYPE/FUNCTION_IDENTITY/FUNCTION_SIGNATURE nodes while iterating normalization.facts, the lossy compatibility projection. Since semantic_observation_fact() returns None for CALL/CONTROL_FLOW/DATA_FLOW/STATE/EFFECT, a future extractor for any of those dimensions would silently never reach the graph until this boundary was fixed -- recreating exactly the parser/extractor-to-graph-bypass .atlas/decisions/0001-one-normalized-semantic-path.md forbids, just one stage later.
defect_4_graph_still_reads_compatibility.fix: New add_typed_semantic_nodes() (core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs) builds these 4 node kinds directly from normalization.typed_semantic_records, matched explicitly per SemanticObservation variant (including the not-yet-real CALL/CONTROL_FLOW/DATA_FLOW/STATE/EFFECT variants as explicit no-op arms, never a wildcard, so a future extractor without a matching graph arm fails to compile instead of silently producing nothing). Node creation for these 4 kinds was removed from the compatibility-facts loop (turned into no-ops); the facts still reach graph.facts for legacy/report bookkeeping, but no longer drive node/edge/binding creation. ensure_node() was refactored to take a &Provenance directly instead of a whole &SemanticFact so both loops can share it. No string is re-parsed to reconstruct typed data anywhere in the new code path.

runtime_invariants_established: record_id() (semantic CLAIM identity) and raw_observation_id() (exact RAW observation identity) are two distinct, independently computed identities; only the latter is ever used to decide whether two raw observations collapse. Two independent extractors reporting the same semantic claim always produce distinct raw_observation_ids (their ExtractorIdentity differs, which participates in the hash) and therefore both survive Census and Normalization untouched.

CensusReport.typed_obligations / NormalizationReport.typed_obligations is a canonical, serializable obligation ledger: for every requested dimension on every extracted artifact, a SemanticObligationRecord exists that resolves its own observation_ids/evidence_refs/diagnostic_ids within the same report, answerable without the original ExtractionBatch[].

is_closed() on both reports now fails if a typed observation or obligation is dropped, or if any evidence/diagnostic/observation cross-reference dangles -- independent of whatever the compatibility facts/facts_total still say.

The engineering graph's SYMBOL/TYPE/FUNCTION_IDENTITY/FUNCTION_SIGNATURE nodes are built directly from NormalizationReport.typed_semantic_records; the compatibility SemanticFact projection for these kinds is provably inert for graph structure (adding/removing it changes graph.facts bookkeeping only, never nodes/edges/bindings).
contract_clauses_satisfied: .atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-EXTRACTION.md#multi-engine-extraction ("Independent extractors MAY analyze the same dimension. Their identities/evidence remain separate ... one extractor may not overwrite another": now literally enforced by raw_observation_id-based dedup, proven by a dedicated multi-extractor regression test that fails under the reverted record_id-only dedup)

.atlas/contracts/NORMALIZATION.md#record-identity ("RawRecordId != NormalizedRecordId": RawObservationId and SemanticRecordId are now two distinct, separately-computed types; normalization dedups by the raw identity, never conflating it with the claim identity)

.atlas/contracts/CENSUS-COMPLETENESS.md (the canonical Census can now answer which extractor evaluated which dimension, for which artifact, at which revision, with what result, and why -- from typed_obligations/typed_semantic_records/evidence/diagnostics alone)

.atlas/decisions/0001-one-normalized-semantic-path.md (no parser/extractor bypass creates canonical semantics; the graph now demonstrably projects from the NORMALIZED typed path, not a lossy string projection, closing the R4.4 sidecar risk this wave targeted)

.atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-EXTRACTION.md#r4-acceptance-matrix ("SemanticFact remains a compatibility envelope, not the only semantic type system": now also true for graph construction, not only Census/Normalization)
still_unsupported: CALL/CONTROL_FLOW/DATA_FLOW/STATE/EFFECT/OWNERSHIP/CONCURRENCY/PERSISTENCE -- no extraction exists for these dimensions yet (R4.4+); this wave did not add any (explicit scope exclusion). The graph boundary is now ready for them (explicit no-op match arms that will force a compile error when a real observation variant needs handling), but no logic for them was added.

Compiler-backed name resolution / TypeIdentity.canonical resolution, rustc/HIR/MIR/trait-solving/macro-expansion/cross-crate resolution, call graph, CFG, dataflow -- none added or required this wave; TypeIdentity.canonical remains None everywhere except the pre-existing unrelated test fixture (core/src/semantic/types.rs).

Normalization remains N0 (deterministic ordering + exact raw-identity/obligation-coordinate collapse only); full stable-identity/equivalence-class/exact-semantic-dedup rules from NORMALIZATION.md are still future R4 work.

Reconciliation of disagreeing extractor results across batches is still explicitly deferred; this wave only ensures every raw observation (agreeing or disagreeing) reaches and survives the canonical typed record set without premature merging.
R4.4 semantic-depth expansion itself -- deliberately not started this wave, per explicit instruction.
acceptance_statement: Atlas Studio now preserves independent extractor observations, obligation/evidence/diagnostic lineage, and typed normalization closure without premature semantic deduplication; the Engineering Graph projects currently-real semantic families directly from normalized typed records, while SemanticFact remains only a compatibility/bootstrap projection.
